newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen buying 92,000T soybeans, 16,000T corn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen buying 92,000T soybeans, 16,000T corn.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected in the market for up to 92,000 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of corn this week, local traders said on Monday.
They said domestic soybean buyers had returned to the market to cover their production needs as many expect to see higher world futures prices ahead.
"Soybean futures remain bullish right now," a buyer at Formosa Oilseed Processing Corp said.

Traders said the Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association would tender soon for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans and Hui Shung Group would retender within a week for a combined shipment of 38,000 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of corn.
They said Taiwan buyers, in general, expect to see U.S. soybean futures reach US$7.60 to US$7.80 per bushel soon.

Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soybean futures closed between 6-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents higher on Friday, supported by strong USDA weekly export sales data and U.S. Census crush figures. The March contract closed up 6-1/4 at $7.47-1/2.
In the wheat market, Taiwan Flour Mills Association official Lu Wei-chih said his association would not be buying this week.
Local listed wheat flour prices on Monday ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 per kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.

Pacific Northwest freight to Taiwan dry bulk freight rates were quoted at about US$14.00 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico in a range between US$22.50 and US$23.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
